issues.current_extraction: Dear Jeffrey, On this occasion, I am reminded of your many conversations, fuelled by both your curiosity and your skepticism. Quoting great minds may be the only gift I can give you to stimulate the one and release the other. First, Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.: 'Certitude is not the test of certainty. We have been cock sure of many things that were just so.' Your curiosity, continuing on with your skepticism, will take care of this without hazard, birthday after birthday. Next, Thoreau: 'Pursue, keep up with, circle round and round your life, as a dog does his master’s chase. Do what you love. Know your own bone; gnaw at it, bury it, unearth it, and gnaw it still.' This too, you do admirably. Then, Leonardo da Vinci: 'Iron rusts from disuse, stagnant water loses its purity and in cold weather becomes frozen; even so does inaction sap the vigor of the mind.' Epstein is not at risk. When he is in the room, you do not fall asleep. Finally, a remark from the not so great Gertrude Stein on your interests: 'As a cousin of mine once said about money, money is always there but the pockets change; it is not in the same pockets after a change, and that is all there is to say about money.' You have said more and, going beyond talk, have shown how to find it. And so, felicitations on the vigors of your body and mind and warm hopes for many occasions celebrating their gifts. Jerry Edelman
